newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline drifts lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline drifts lower in thin trade.

text.p: HOUSTON, Jan 3 (Reuter) U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices drifted slightly lower in thin trade on Friday as operations at regional refineries returned to normal, traders said.
"There's not much of anything going on today," one trader said, adding that discussion was expected to pick up next week as traders returned from the holidays.
Severe storms in the Pacific Northwest idled at least one regional refinery on the week, but as the storms abated traders and refinery officials said production was returning to normal.
"We are in normal operations," a spokesman for Texaco's 136,000 barrel per day Anacortes, Wash., refinery said.
CARB gasoline eased 0.50 cent to bids 79 cents a gallon in Los Angeles and was unchanged at 79/80 cents in San Francisco, traders said. CARB premium remained 3 cents a gallon higher.
